Answer: C
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a massive, well-circumscribed opacity occupying the right hemithorax with smooth borders and no mediastinal shift, which is characteristic of a large pleural-based tumor like a liposarcoma rather than an effusion (which would typically cause contralateral shift at this size) or pneumonia. The subsequent image (Figure 1c) showing clear lungs after intervention confirms the mass was a resectable solid lesion, consistent with a sarcoma.
